newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - June 19.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Under moves indicating its senior management problems, the ANZ Banking Group has undergone restructuring. Soon to retire chief executive Don Mercer will conduct a strategic review and would have filled the newly created second-in-command role as head of global retail banking. Page 1.

The announcement yesterday by former Queensland Labor Premier Wayne Goss that he plans to move into Federal politics was welcomed by Federal Opposition Leader Kim Beazley, who said he would immediately give Goss a front-bench berth. Page 3.

Federal Government plans for a convention on the republic are in confusion after the Senate rejected the proposed voluntary postal ballot to elect half the delegates. The Government responded to the rejection by saying it would not accept the change when the legislation returned to the House of Representatives. Page 4.

The Australian Federal Police expect further problems in obtaining information from Swiss businessman Jurg Bollag about his business dealings with Australian entrepreneur Alan Bond. Bollag, whose evidence is critical to ascertain whether Bond breached th Bankruptcy Act in 1995, refused to give evidence to Swiss prosecutor Paul Kuhn, who was acting on behalf of the Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions in April. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The future of the Constitutional Convention on the republic is in doubt after the Senate rejected the Federal Government's plans for deciding on a republic. The Government has threatened to dump the convention, or remove the rights of voters to elect their members, a move that prompted the Opposition, Democrats and the Australian Republican Movement to warn of a boycott. Page 1.

National Party Senate Leader Ron Boswell told the Senate yesterday Pauline Hanson's One Nation Party has been infiltrated by right-wing groups with links to violent and racist groups. Boswell said One Nation members in Newcastle and Queensland had links with the League of Rights and a number of extremist publications. Page 1.

The emergence of new technology, such as telephones, fax machines and electronic messages, has seen a drop in the number of personal letters being sent through the post. Last year, postal mail accounted for less than one-fifth of the 20.5 billion messages sent in Australia, and deliveries of personal mail by Australia Post has dropped 50 per cent in eight years. Page 1.

Labor Senator Stephen Conroy, who was last week attacked by former Elders IXL head John Elliott during a parliamentary inquiry into the National Crime Authority, yesterday released previously secret NCA evidence. Conroy has suggested Elliott and his collague Peter Scanlon had prior knowledge of a controversial transaction that was under investigation. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

While not confirming the plan, it is believed Toyota will build a V6-powered family and fleet Australian-made car to take on the Falcon and Commodore. Plans for the new car, called Avalon, have been stepped up following the Federal Government's decision on car tariffs. Page 1.

Independent Senator Brian Harradine yesterday sided with the ALP, the Australian Democrats and the Greens to vote down the Federal Government's plans for voluntary postal vote for the constitutional convention on the republic, voting instead for a full compulsory ballot to elect half of the delegates. Page 1.

Senator Steve Conroy yesterday read to Federal Parliament details of a transcript of evidence given to the National Crime Authority linking former Elders IXL head John Elliott to a A$66.5 million payment, the subject of the largest corporate fraud trial in Australia. Page 1.

The China Bowl restaurant in the Sydney suburb of Coogee has been linked to at least nine cases of hepatitis A, with one victim in a serious condition. The New South Wales Department of Health is still searching for the cause of the outbreak, with the restaurant denying it would be the source. Page 3.
THE AGE

Victorian Labor Senator Stephen Conroy yesterday revealed controversial information withheld from the trial of businessman John Elliott in Federal Parliament, after last week being unable to disclose the material at a joint parliamentary National Crime Authority committee hearing. Page 1.

Researchers from the Victorian Forensic Science Centre, led by Roland van Oorschot and Maxwell Jones, have found that fingerprints contain enough information to identify the total physical make-up of a person, including the colour of their hair. The discovery will be a vital new tool for police investigators. Page 1.

A solicitor acting for Greg Domaszewicz, who was babysitting 14-month-old Jaidyn Leskie the night he was abducted, says the 28-year-old will provide a blood sample for police as soon as possible. Jaidyn was last seen with Domaszewicz on Saturday afternoon while his mother, Belinda Murphy, attended a function in Traralgon. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard will tonight attend the second cricket Test between Australia and England at Lord's, a move that will prompt inevitable comparisons between him and former Prime Minister Sir Robert Menzies. Menzies viewed cricket as a diversion and hated talking politics while watching play. Page 1.
